construct: display: flex; align-items: center — cross-axis centring of two children of DIFFERENT heights
why: align-items is the cross-axis half of the flex vocabulary and one of the four layout facts the whole CSS->Figma lowering reframe rests on. It was classified CARRIED on a code citation alone; until 2026-08-26 the fixture's reader could not observe it at all (carriage was recorded under the contract's field name `align`, a spelling no browser emits), so no case could ever have caught it. The children differ in height on purpose: with equal heights, `center` and `stretch` draw the same picture and the case would prove nothing.
